msg: Hola, buen día. Somos un grupo de 7 amigas de Bogotá. Tres ya tenemos el Open Water, dos quieren probar el minicurso y dos prefieren snorkel. ¿Cuánto saldría por persona saliendo desde Cartagena y hay descuento por grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Buen día! ¡Qué chévere plan para las siete! Sí, pueden combinar buceo para certificadas, minicurso y snorkel en la misma salida. Para las tres buceadoras certificadas, el plan desde Cartagena requiere **dos inmersiones**; el precio te lo dejo a continuación.

El descuento de grupo es del **10% para grupos de 5 o más** y aplica al minicurso y al snorkel, pero no a cursos PADI. Se suma al descuento online y hay que solicitarlo antes de pagar.

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
• Minicurso de Buceo: 655.000 COP · 727.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 448.000 COP · 497.000 COP

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

¿Quieres que te ayude a continuar con la reserva?

Snorkeling in the Rosario Islands is a lovely way to spend your day. So, would you leave *from Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. - The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). msg: Solo yo. ¿A qué hora me recogerían en el Cocoliso y tengo que llevar algo? Gracias.
reply:
En Cocoliso, la recogida es entre las 9:30 y las 9:45. Lleva tu bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo está incluido. También debes presentar tu carné de buceo; puedes mostrarlo el día de la actividad o enviar una foto antes. 🌊

También necesitas:
• Estar listo a las 9:30 en tu hotel
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

msg: Good afternoon. I am from Germany and I hold an Open Water certification, although I have not dived for three years. I am staying in Getsemaní and I would like to dive next Wednesday. My flight home leaves on Thursday at 22:00. Is this possible, and what would you recommend?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

From your flight time, you can dive **up to Wednesday** and still fly on **Thursday at 22:00**. The minimum wait after recreational diving is **18 hours**, so that flight is fine. 🌊

Since you have **Open Water** and it has been **three years** since your last dive, the best recommendation is the **Refresher**. It is designed for certified divers who have been out of the water for more than 2 years, and it is booked as the **Dive Mini Course**.

Booking is done through the online link, and for this plan the Cartagena link is:

https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en

If you’d like, I can also help you compare it with a regular fun dive option for certified divers.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Hey! I'm an American diver, Advanced Open Water. I'm renting a house on Airbnb on Isla Grande next week, it's called Villa Marea. I'd like to do two dives. Can you pick me up there? How does that work?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a great plan! For two certified dives while you’re already on Isla Grande, pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge **if your accommodation has maritime access**. Pick-up is usually between **9:30 and 9:45 a.m.**; the boat may come directly to the house, or you may need to meet at a nearby dock.

Since Villa Marea is an Airbnb and isn’t on our listed hotel locations, a team advisor needs to confirm the pick-up arrangements before you book and pay. Would you like me to connect you with an advisor to check Villa Marea’s access?

msg: Gracias. Nos interesa el minicurso, para los dos. ¿A qué profundidad se baja? Y mi esposa pregunta si hace falta saber nadar muy bien, porque ella nada lo justo. Quisiéramos ir el sábado 14 de noviembre.
reply:
El minicurso llega hasta los **12 metros**; lo habitual es bucear entre 5 y 12 metros. No hace falta tener experiencia previa. Sobre saber nadar, no tengo ese requisito confirmado para el minicurso; como tu esposa nada lo justo, es mejor que lo confirme un asesor antes de reservar.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 12 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

🤿 *Minicurso de Buceo*
💰 *655.000 COP* por persona · 2 personas

El pago es en pesos colombianos (COP): pueden pagar *100 % online* o un *anticipo del 50 %* con el enlace, el QR o Llave que envía el asesor, y el *otro 50 % el día de la actividad*.

msg: Perfecto, gracias, espero entonces lo del asma. Mientras tanto, otra duda: tengo que estar en Bogotá el lunes para trabajar. Si hago el curso sábado y domingo, ¿puedo coger un vuelo el domingo por la noche, cuando vuelva a Cartagena? Y sobre la teoría, ¿tengo que estudiar algo antes de ir?
reply:
Para el Curso Open Water, la teoría se hace antes en PADI eLearning y debes completarla para empezar la práctica; toma aproximadamente 10 a 12 horas.

Sobre el vuelo: debes esperar al menos 18 horas desde la última inmersión. El curso termina el domingo con las inmersiones finales, así que un vuelo esa misma noche no cumple ese intervalo. El regreso a Cartagena no cambia el tiempo de espera.

También necesitas:
• Con este plan debes alojarte al menos 1 noche en las Islas del Rosario (hotel no incluido)
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

Para preguntas médicas específicas, es importante que hables con nuestro staff calificado para evaluar tu situación particular. Te paso ahora con alguien del equipo, que te escribe por aquí enseguida.

msg: Hey! Planning a bachelor party in Cartagena in February, there will be 6 of us from Texas. Three of the guys are certified and three have never dived. We want one day out on the water together. What's the deal price-wise for a group like ours? And can we pay with US credit cards? One of us would pay for everybody.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a great one-day outing in the Rosario Islands! The three certified divers can do the two-dive Fun Dives, while the three who haven’t dived can choose a Dive Mini Course, snorkeling, or come along on the boat as companions.

For the certified divers, the Cartagena price is **$178 online or $197 regular per person**. The Dive Mini Course is **$183 online or $204 regular per person**. I’m leaving the prices below as well.

Your group qualifies for an extra **10% group discount**, which stacks with the **10% online discount** for eligible activities. The group discount must be requested before paying; it isn’t applied automatically. You can pay by US credit card on the website, and one person can pay for the group. International guests pay in full by card online; with a foreign card, use a passport as the ID document.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

Would you like to book the certified dives and mini-courses as separate activities?

msg: Good call on asking: one of the certified guys, Mike, last dived about three years ago. The other two dived last summer. No beers, got it. So what does Mike need to do? And who do I talk to on your team to get the group discount before we pay?
reply:
Mike is still a certified diver, but since it’s been about three years, a refresher is normally required. - Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.

Other ways to ask: Can I dive if I fly out tomorrow morning? / I don't have much time, what can I do before I leave? / What time does it finish so I can leave?
Answer: If you leave the next day around noon: from the Rosario Islands it is very tight (pickup is between 9:30 and 9:45 and the activity ends around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), so it is best to confirm it with a team advisor; departing from Cartagena it does not fit (the boat returns at 3:00 p.m. and arrives around 4:15 p.m.). Question: What are my options if I don't want to do the night dive included in the package?
Other ways to ask: Can I swap the night dive for only daytime dives in my package? / What should I do if I don't want the night dive included in my package?
Answer: If you do not wish to do the night dive included in the packages, you can choose the 4 Daytime Dives Package, which consists of 4 daytime dives over 2 days, with no night dive. This package is available both for departures from Cartagena and for those already on the islands. In the 5, 7, and 9 dive packages, the night dive is included; if you prefer not to do it, the alternative is to switch to the 4 Daytime Dives Package.

Other ways to ask: Is it possible to book just one dive departing from Cartagena? / Do you offer the option of a single dive from Cartagena?
Answer: From Cartagena, the minimum is 2 dives (a full-day trip), as the boat logistics and trip timing do not allow for a single dive. [7] Fuente: policies
Question: How long do I have to wait to fly after diving?
Other ways to ask: Can I fly the same day I dive? / What's the minimum time between diving and flying?
Answer: Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.

Question: What time does the activity finish?

Answer: All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).

Question: Is diving safe?
Other ways to ask: Is it safe to go diving? / Are there risks in diving or is it considered safe?
Answer: Yes, diving is safe when procedures and training limits are followed. The basic rules are: never hold your breath, ascend slowly, always dive with a buddy, equalize early and often, respect depth limits, constantly monitor your air, and follow the instructor or guide. The bot can give general guidance, but it cannot clear someone medically or replace a dive professional's judgment.

[10] Fuente: faqs
Question: Are fish, sharks, starfish, coral, or sea urchins dangerous?
Other ways to ask: Is it dangerous to encounter sharks, fish, or sea urchins while diving? / Should I be concerned about marine animals like coral or starfish when diving?
Answer: Most fish avoid humans. If you see a shark, the recommended approach is to stay calm, observe, and enjoy the moment from a respectful distance; encounters are usually safe. Touching starfish, turtles, coral, or any organism is not recommended: many are delicate or sensitive. Many minor diving injuries occur from accidental contact with coral or sea urchins, which is why neutral buoyancy and not touching anything are fundamental for safety.

msg: Hiya! I'm Priya, a British backpacker on a tight budget, currently in Santa Marta and heading to Cartagena next week. I've got three free days, November 17 to 19, and I've always wanted to get my diving certification. Is that doable in three days, and what's the cheapest way of doing it? I've got a hostel in Getsemaní booked already.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Hiya, Priya! Getting certified is a fantastic way to experience the Rosario Islands. The Open Water course takes two days, so it fits within your three free days, November 17–19. You’ll need to stay overnight on the islands after day one; your Getsemaní hostel won’t cover that, and accommodation there isn’t included.

The course includes online theory, pool sessions and four certification dives. From Cartagena, you meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on day one and return around 4:15 p.m. on day two. The online rate is the cheapest listed, and I’m leaving the prices below.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

Would you like to book the Open Water course?

msg: Brilliant. How long does the online theory take, and when do I get access to it? I'd have about a week to do it. Also, I need somewhere cheap to sleep on the island for that one night: do you know a budget option? And would I save anything by going to the island the day before and starting from there?
reply:
The Open Water theory takes about **10–12 hours** and must be completed before the practical training. You’ll get access to PADI eLearning after enrolling, so a week should give you time to work through it.

Accommodation isn’t included, and you book directly with the hotel. I don’t have current budget rates, but nearby options with maritime access include Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Our base hotels are San Pedro de Majagua and Cocoliso on Isla Grande.

Going to the islands a day early doesn’t reduce the course price: the Cartagena course already includes round-trip boat transport, while the island-based course has a different price because it excludes that transport and lunch. The island-based option requires you to have booked your hotel first.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Hi! We're two certified divers visiting Cartagena next week from Chicago. Do you run dive trips to the Rosario Islands?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Yes, we do! 🐠 Diving the Rosario Islands is a beautiful experience — a protected archipelago with coral reefs, warm Caribbean water year-round, and relaxed profiles, just 45–60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.

For certified divers departing from Cartagena, the classic option is **Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day)**:
- 2 guided reef dives with a PADI professional
- Same-day round trip from Cartagena (boat Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena)
- Lunch included, plus park entrance fee, dive insurance and full gear
- 178 USD / 630.000 COP online (197 USD / 700.000 COP regular)

The day starts at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. and you're back in Cartagena around 4:15 p.m.

If you'd like more diving, there are also multi-day packages (2, 3 or 4 days) that include a night dive and require staying overnight on the islands.

One thing to keep in mind: you'll need to bring your certification card, and if it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required.

Would you like me to help you set up the booking?

msg: Do you pick us up at the hotel? What time, and do we need to bring our own gear?
reply:
Yes—pick-up and return by boat at Cocoliso are included at no extra charge. The pick-up is usually between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m.; the exact time and meeting point are coordinated with the team. Diving and snorkeling gear are included, so you don’t need to bring your own. Bring a swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes.

You'll also need:
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.

Shall we go for the *2-dive trip* for you and, for your companion, the *mini-course*, *snorkeling* or just coming along on the *boat*? 🌊

msg: Hi, I'm a German traveler in Cartagena and I've never dived. I'd like to get my Open Water certification. How long does the course take?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

The Open Water course takes **2 days** and certifies you to dive down to **18 m**. It’s a great way to start diving! 🌊

From Cartagena, you meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on Day 1. The course includes online PADI theory, pool sessions, and four certification dives across the two days. You’ll need to stay overnight on the islands after Day 1; accommodation isn’t included and is booked directly with the hotel. You return to Cartagena on Day 2 at 3:00 p.m. (estimated arrival around 4:15 p.m.).

The online price is **USD 693 per person** (regular price: **USD 770**). Would you like the booking link?

msg: ¿Ella puede hacer algo en el agua? ¿Y necesitaría algún permiso médico?
reply:
Sí, puede hacer snorkel en superficie, con el visto bueno de su médico. Durante el embarazo no se recomienda bucear con botella.

También necesitas:
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.

No tenemos un permiso médico específico para el snorkel; sí es importante que cuente con la aprobación de su médico. 🌊

¿Te animas con la *salida de 2 inmersiones*, un *paquete de varios días* o un *curso avanzado*? 🌊

msg: Tell me about the 3-dive package with a night dive. Where would I sleep and is the hotel included?
reply:
The 3-dive package is a great one — 2 daytime dives plus a night dive, and the night dive in the Rosario Islands is a really special experience. 🌙

Here's how it works: you head out from Cartagena in the morning, do your 2 daytime dives with a surface interval and lunch, and then the night dive. Because of the night dive, you can't do it as a same-day round trip — you stay overnight on the islands and return to Cartagena the next day on our boat (it leaves the base at 3:00 p.m.).

The hotel is *not* included — you book your accommodation directly with the hotel. Our base is at two hotels on Isla Grande: Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso. Other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao.

It includes the National Park entrance fee, dive insurance, speedboat transport Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena, 3 guided dives with a PADI professional, diving equipment and lunch.

One thing to keep in mind: since it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required, and it takes its own day — so the dive trip can't be done the same day.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
*From Cartagena* — boat from Muelle de la Bodeguita · lunch included (on multi-day plans, the first day's)
• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 287 USD · 319 USD
• 5 Dives - 2 days: 392 USD · 436 USD
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch
• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 188 USD · 209 USD
• 5-dive package (2 days): 319 USD · 354 USD

Would you leave *from Cartagena* or are you already *on the Rosario Islands*? Then I'll give you the exact plan. 🌊

msg: Do I need a refresher since it's been so long? And how do I book?
reply:
Yes—since it’s been more than two years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required. It’s a mini-course with a pool session and one dive with an instructor, and it takes a separate day, so you can’t do the refresher and the dive trip on the same day. If you’ve already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another center, that counts. Very experienced divers with 500+ dives or Dive Master level are reviewed by the team.

You can book the refresher online here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en. The 10% online discount is applied automatically. The website closes bookings for the next day at 4:30 p.m.; since it’s already past that time, you can book for the next available day. Please bring your certified diver card. The refresher also requires the course medical form: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Hola, soy colombiana, vivo en Bogotá y me alojo en un hotel en Barú con mi madre. Queremos hacer snorkel un día, ¿es posible?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

Sí, ¡es posible hacer snorkel por un día! Como te alojas en Barú, la salida es desde Cartagena, en el Muelle de la Bodeguita; no hacemos recogidas en Barú.

El tour incluye transporte en lancha, equipo de snorkel, dos salidas guiadas, almuerzo, seguro y entrada al Parque Nacional. El encuentro es a las 8:00 a. m. y el regreso a Cartagena está previsto para las 4:15 p. m.

🤿 *Tour de Snorkeling*
💰 *448.000 COP* por persona · 2 personas

El pago es en pesos colombianos (COP): pueden pagar *100 % online* o un *anticipo del 50 %* con el enlace, el QR o Llave que envía el asesor, y el *otro 50 % el día de la actividad*.

¿Quieren que les pase con un asesor para reservar y coordinar el pago? 🌊

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

msg: Un detalle: mi esposo buceó por última vez en abril de 2022 y yo en enero de este año, en Capurganá. ¿Eso cambia algo para él?
reply:
Sí, para él cambia: como su última inmersión fue en abril de 2022, normalmente se requiere un *refresh* antes de volver a bucear. El refresher se reserva como Minicurso de Buceo y ocupa su propio día; ese día no se hace la salida de buceo. Como estarán varios días, puede hacer el refresh el primero y bucear los demás. Si ya hizo un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como su refresh y puede bucear directamente. Para buzos muy experimentados, con más de 500 inmersiones o nivel Dive Master, un asesor revisa si hace falta.

También necesitas:
• Ser buzo certificado y presentar tu carnet
• Con este plan debes alojarte 1 noche en las Islas del Rosario (hotel no incluido)
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

🤿 *Paquete de 4 inmersiones (2 días, 4 diurnas)*
💰 *1.154.000 COP* por persona · 2 personas

El pago es en pesos colombianos (COP): pueden pagar *100 % online* o un *anticipo del 50 %* con el enlace, el QR o Llave que envía el asesor, y el *otro 50 % el día de la actividad*.

¿Quieren que les pase con un asesor para reservar y coordinar el pago? 🌊

msg: ¿Qué incluye cada salida? Queremos saber si hay que llevar almuerzo y si el transporte hasta el muelle corre por nuestra cuenta.

- Lancha rápida Cartagena–Islas del Rosario–Cartagena.

El alojamiento en las islas, las fotos o videos submarinos, las propinas y la comida adicional tampoco están incluidos.

msg: Great, thanks. So the plan would be: my husband diving, our 11-year-old trying scuba for the first time, and me and our 6-year-old snorkeling, all on December 3 from Hotel Cocoliso. We're US citizens. How do we book and pay?
reply:
Perfect! For December 3 from Hotel Cocoliso, you can book the activities online. Your husband can book certified fun dives, your 11-year-old can book the Dive Mini Course, and you and your 6-year-old can book snorkeling. Pick the date and number of people in each activity’s booking link:

- **Certified fun dives:** https://book.divingplanet.org/book/fun-dives-already-on-island/19?language=en
- **Dive Mini Course:** https://book.divingplanet.org/book/dive-mini-course-already-on-island/20?language=en
- **Snorkeling:** https://book.divingplanet.org/book/snorkeling-already-on-the-island/25?language=en

As US citizens, you’ll pay in USD by card on the website. The 10% online discount is applied automatically. Payment is recorded right away, then the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking. If you use a foreign card, use your passport as the ID document. Hotel Cocoliso pickup is included.

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

For the one who hasn't chosen yet I'd recommend these options. Which one do they like best? 🐠
• *Certified diving* — Guided dives for already-certified divers; explore the reef at depth.
• *Dive mini-course* — A first time underwater with an instructor: pool training and a real dive. No experience needed.
• *Snorkeling* — Enjoy the reef from the surface, with mask and fins. Great for families.
• *Come along as a companion* — Comes on the boat and enjoys the day with the group, without getting in the water.

msg: ¿Los niños pueden bucear con esas edades? Al de 9 le encanta el mar, pero no sé si es muy chico para el minicurso.
reply:
¡Sí, los dos pueden disfrutar del mar! Con 9 años, puede hacer *snorkel* (desde los 6) o *Bubble Makers*, una experiencia introductoria en piscina o aguas muy poco profundas, máximo 2 m, con un instructor dedicado. El minicurso es desde los 10 años.

Con 13 años, puede hacer snorkel, minicurso, Open Water, Advanced o Rescue. Para las salidas como buzo certificado necesita tener certificación Open Water. Los menores deben ir acompañados por un adulto responsable.

Si quieres, te ayudo a reservar: *Minicurso de buceo*. ¿Te animas? 🌊

msg: Gracias. Entonces sería el domingo 13 de diciembre desde Cartagena: mi esposo a bucear, el de 13 y yo al minicurso, y para el de 9 lo que le corresponda por su edad. ¿Cómo hacemos la reserva y cuánto hay que pagar por adelantado?
reply:
¡Qué buen plan familiar! Para el de 9 años, las opciones son *snorkel* o *Bubble Makers*; el minicurso es desde los 10 años. Tu esposo puede hacer buceo certificado si tiene certificación Open Water. Ojo: el minicurso no certifica, así que quienes lo hagan no pueden sumarse a las inmersiones de buceo certificado durante ese viaje ni al día siguiente.

El snorkel cuesta *126 USD online* y Bubble Makers para niños de 8 a 10 años cuesta *168 USD online*. Reservando online se aplica automáticamente el 10% de descuento. Como pagan en dólares, se paga el 100% al reservar con tarjeta extranjera en la página web, usando el pasaporte como documento de identificación.

Minicurso: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=es  
Buceo certificado: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=es  
Snorkel: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/superficio/3?language=es  

Bubble Makers no tiene enlace online; para reservarlo, ¿quieres que te pase con un asesor del equipo?

Siempre hay disponibilidad: operamos todos los días, festivos incluidos, salvo el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero; si el mar no está apto, la salida se reprograma.

🤿

msg: ¿Cómo es el curso Open Water con ustedes? ¿Cuántos días dura, hay que estudiar algo antes y se puede ir y volver a Cartagena cada día?
reply:
¡Es una experiencia buenísima para empezar a bucear! El Open Water dura **2 días** e incluye teoría online PADI eLearning, entrenamiento en piscina y **4 inmersiones en aguas abiertas**. La teoría toma aproximadamente **10 a 12 horas** y debes completarla antes de empezar la parte práctica.

No se puede ir y volver a Cartagena cada día: deben alojarse **al menos una noche en las islas**; el alojamiento no está incluido y se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Saliendo desde Cartagena, el día 1 se encuentran a las **8:00 a. m. en el Muelle de la Bodeguita**. Hacen piscina y dos inmersiones; después van al hotel en las islas. El día 2 completan la piscina y las dos inmersiones finales, y regresan a Cartagena a las **3:00 p. m.**, con llegada aproximada a las **4:15 p. m.** El almuerzo está incluido el primer día, no el segundo.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

¿Saldrías *desde Cartagena* o ya estás *en las Islas del Rosario*? Así te paso el plan exacto. 🌊

msg: Bárbaro. Somos dos argentinos y queremos el curso Open Water el 2 y el 3 de diciembre desde Cartagena. ¿Cómo reservamos y pagamos?
reply:
¡De una! Para reservar el Curso Open Water para el 2 y 3 de diciembre desde Cartagena, elijan la fecha y las 2 personas en este enlace: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/basic-course/4?language=es

Como son clientes extranjeros, el pago es del **100% en línea con tarjeta extranjera**; usen el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El pago se registra al momento y el equipo lo concilia poco después para confirmar la reserva. Si falla el sistema o el pago online, el equipo les enviará un enlace para pagar por transferencia.

La reserva online incluye automáticamente el **10% de descuento**. Recuerden que el curso requiere alojarse al menos una noche en las islas; el alojamiento se reserva aparte directamente con el hotel.

Quien no es colombiano ni residente en Colombia paga en dólares (USD) con tarjeta en la web; la tarifa es la misma, solo cambia la moneda.

msg: Since we're a group of five, is there a group discount? Also, can we bring a few beers on the boat for after the dives?
reply:
Yes. There’s a **10% group discount for groups of 5 or more**, and it stacks with the **10% online discount** for a total of **20% when booking online**. It applies to recreational diving and snorkeling, but it isn’t automatic: the group discount must be requested from the team **before paying**. If you pay without requesting it, it can’t be refunded afterward. Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to request it?

**No alcohol is allowed on the boat or during the activity**, so you can’t bring beers for after the dives. Please also avoid alcohol before diving and make sure you’re in good physical condition.
